about.title: Yucaipa Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Yucaipa's mix of local streets and freeway access makes for a lot of daily traffic movement, and with that comes crashes. Public records show 151 injury collisions in the most recent full year, with 218 people hurt and 4 lives lost — numbers that reflect a community where cars, cyclists, and pedestrians share busy corridors like Bryant Street and Yucaipa Boulevard. Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. see a noticeable rise in reported crashes, likely tied to end-of-week commute and errand traffic. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memories can fade. We handle personal injury claims for injured Yucaipa residents and can evaluate what happened and explain your options, at no cost to start.
commonInjuries: Torn ligaments and soft tissue damage

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Fault Rules Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault system, you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault — we can help make sure your share of blame isn't overstated.

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a claim, but it can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a public road agency — is involved, so early action matters.

items.title: What You Say Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: Insurers often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash; we can guide you on what to say (or not say) since there's no cap on non-economic damages you may be entitled to pursue.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Yucaipa?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That window can shrink to as little as six months if your claim involves a government entity, such as a city road department. We can confirm the deadline that applies to your specific situation.

items.question: Should I give the insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement to any insurer, including your own, before speaking with an attorney. Statements made early on can be used later to minimize your claim. We can advise you on what information you're required to share.

items.question: What if the crash happened on I-10 or another busy Yucaipa corridor and fault is disputed?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you're found partially responsible for a crash on roads like I-10 or Yucaipa Boulevard. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. We can help gather evidence to fairly represent what happened.

items.question: Do you charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost to you to contact us and discuss your situation.
